description: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics — “Initial Acc,” “Δ Acc,” and an unlabeled blue line — across five discrete initial confidence levels ranging from 0.95 to 0.99. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” is linear and spans from 0.95 to 0.99 with tick marks at 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, and 0.99. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” is linear and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines at intervals of 0.2. The blue solid line with circle markers starts at approximately 0.88 at 0.95 initial confidence, rises slightly to a peak of ~0.91 at 0.98, then declines to ~0.87 at 0.99. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, labeled “Δ Acc,” begins at ~0.89 at 0.95, remains relatively flat until 0.98 (~0.87), then drops sharply to ~0.75 at 0.99. The green dash-dotted line with square markers, labeled “Initial Acc,” remains near zero across all confidence levels, rising slightly from 0.0 at 0.95 to ~0.12 at 0.99. Error bars are present on all data points, indicating variability, with larger vertical error bars on the green line at higher confidence levels. The legend includes a gray rectangle with no label, which does not correspond to any plotted line.
